searchText: Soliciting feedback for the `eth_fillTransaction` spec. https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/512 And yet these methods are used widely in the clients. There are other classes of users to a client than a dapp. The UX of `eth_fillTransaction` is IMO much better as the output of that can be taken directly to the signer. I think introducing a new method for blob proofs is worse UX. I agree that `eth_fillTransaction` is useful. My argument is only that it shouldn't be a requirement to properly implement an Ethereum Client's JSON-RPC. I would rather see such useful code be put into a library or something and have Ethereum Clients focus only on the lowest-level of interactions with the underlying blockchain. I can stand behind a way to spec "optional" API methods. They already exist in some form. E.g. `trace_` namespace is implemented and agreed on by most clients, but not all (geth is the outlier here). But not specced. I think we're losing out by not having a spec for those. I have another hot spec topic for you guys today it's about `debug_getRawReceipts` I have noticed in hive tests that besu, nethermind and reth return the RLP encoding of receipts from `debug_getRawReceipts` go-ethereum returns the 'consensus encoding', ie. `tx-type || payload` which one is correct? we generally use the 'consensus encoding' in the RPC spec for eth_sendRawTransaction, we use the consensus encoding I think it should be the consensus encoding. I think I implemented the besu version so probably just screwed that up. I think same. But it's 3 against 1 currently. Though, to be fair, rpc-compat tests are still totally broken for erigon, nimbus and ethereumjs. So maybe it's actually 3 vs 3 Pretty sure geth was first though... Plus I'm not sure you can reliably parse the different receipt types without having the leading byte.
